tasks.short: Notice signs of abuse or family problems, talk with the student or parents, follow the reporting code, consult the advice line, refer to mental health help and record each step.

steps.what: Counselor notices signs or hears teachers' concerns about domestic abuse or family problems
Counselor talks with the student or parents and encourages them to seek additional assistance
Counselor looks up the steps of the reporting code in the school binder
Counselor phones the national advice line for domestic abuse to consult
Counselor refers the student or parents to mental health professionals and helps make the first appointment
Counselor writes concerns, consultations and decisions in the student's file

tasks.design: The steps of the school's reporting code for domestic abuse sit as a checklist in the student guidance system ({OTHER}), where the counselor ticks each step with date and a short note, so the file record builds as the steps are taken. Noticing, talking, consulting the advice line and referring stay fully in person and by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: The reporting code lived in a binder and the record was written afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Guidance systems hold checklists with restricted access.
tasks.still_hard: Every case is different; the checklist must not replace professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Earning enough trust that a frightened student tells what is happening at home.

reach.learn: Whether checklists show where cases stall.

evidence.claim: Schools must follow a reporting code with set steps when abuse is suspected.
Notes on family problems and health are special-category data that need strict access.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing signs to the referral recorded; the advice line's and care providers' work is outside.
Input contract: reporting code checklist kept by the school care coordinator; fallback is the binder.
Talking, consulting and referring do not change.
Access to these records is limited to the care team.
research_questions: Are reporting code steps followed more completely with a checklist?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is noticing and talking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather the student's results and notes, pick participants and times, send invitations, meet parents and teachers, record agreements and send them out.

steps.what: Counselor gathers grades, attendance and notes from several systems before the meeting
Counselor chooses who should attend and finds possible times by e-mail
Counselor e-mails invitations and reminders to parents and teachers
Counselor confers with parents, teachers and administrators to discuss children's progress and resolve problems
Counselor writes agreed priorities and resource needs in the student's file
Counselor e-mails the agreed actions to parents and teachers

tasks.design: The student information system ({OTHER}) shows one overview per student (grades, attendance, earlier agreements) for the counselor to read before the meeting. The counselor picks participants and slots, and the booking tool sends invitations and reminders; after the meeting the counselor records the agreements in fixed fields, and once the counselor marks the record final the system sends the agreed actions to the participants. The meeting itself stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was pulled from several systems and meetings and follow-ups were arranged by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems give one view per student and send messages to parents and staff.
tasks.still_hard: Agreements about a child are sensitive and must reach only the participants.
tasks.human_edge: Getting parents and teachers who blame each other to agree on what the child needs.

evidence.claim: Student information systems give one overview per student and send messages to parents and staff.
Information about a child's problems can be special-category data; share it only with the people who need it.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing the meeting to agreements shared; carrying out the actions is outside.
Input contract: grades and attendance from the student administration; agreement fields set by the guidance team; participant addresses from the student record; fallback is e-mail.
Parents' and teachers' time is outside the counselor's savings.
research_questions: Are agreed actions carried out more often when sent to all participants?

incremental.description: Counselor marks the agreement record final before sending.

approvals.approved_version: The agreement record as marked final by the counselor in s5; later edits are sent as a new version only after a new mark.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Schools with one simple student system already have the overview.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose a prevention programme, arrange dates and speakers, teach the classes, collect evaluations and tally them.

steps.what: Counselor searches for alcohol and drug prevention and conflict programs and materials
Counselor arranges dates and guest speakers with teachers
Counselor teaches classes that help students handle conflicts without violence
Counselor hands out and collects paper evaluation forms
Counselor tallies the evaluation forms

tasks.design: The counselor chooses from a national database of recognised prevention programmes with their materials instead of searching widely. Students fill in a short online survey at the end of class instead of paper forms, and the survey tool tallies the results; arranging dates and teaching stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programmes were found by searching, and evaluations were paper forms counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: National databases list recognised youth interventions; online surveys tally themselves.
tasks.still_hard: Programmes must fit the school's students; survey answers on drugs are sensitive.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a class of teenagers to talk honestly about pressure and conflict.

reach.learn: Whether shared programmes keep lessons consistent.

evidence.claim: National databases list recognised youth interventions with materials.
Survey answers about drug use can be health data; collect them without names.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing a programme to the evaluation summary; school policy is outside.
Input contract: programme database kept by the national youth institute; survey set up by the counselor without names; fallback is web search and paper forms.
Arranging dates and teaching do not change.
research_questions: Do recognised programmes get better evaluations?

incremental.description: Counselor sets up the survey once per programme.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Schools that repeat one programme every year search little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree behaviour rules with staff, write the policy, get management approval, publish it, deal with breaches, record them and spot repeat cases.

steps.what: Counselor discusses rules governing student behavior with management and teachers
Counselor writes the behaviour policy text
School management approves the behaviour policy
Counselor publishes the rules in the handbook and on the website
Counselor enforces administration policies with students who break the rules
Counselor writes breaches and measures in the student's file
Counselor goes through files to spot students with repeated breaches

tasks.design: Breaches and measures are recorded with fixed fields in the student information system ({OTHER}), and a rule alerts the counselor when a student reaches three breaches in a month. The approved policy is published from one source to the handbook and the school website ({CMS}); agreeing the rules, management's approval and dealing with students stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Breaches were free-text notes and repeats were found by reading files.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems record incidents with fields and can alert on counts.
tasks.still_hard: An alert on counts says nothing about why; measures need judgement and fairness.
tasks.human_edge: Enforcing a rule in a way the student can accept.

reach.learn: Whether count alerts help act earlier.

evidence.claim: Student information systems record incidents with fields and alert on counts.
A count-based alert is a plain rule, not AI that evaluates students.

assumptions: Boundary: from agreeing rules to spotting repeat breaches; disciplinary hearings are outside.
Input contract: incident fields and the alert threshold set by school management; fallback is free-text notes.
Management time is outside the counselor's savings.
Dealing with students does not change.
research_questions: Do repeat cases get attention earlier with alerts?

approvals.approved_version: The behaviour policy text approved by school management in s3; any change needs a new approval before publishing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meetings and dealing with students.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The career counselor keeps the sensitive conversations, the classes and the judgement; looking things up, tallying and sending summaries shrink.
reach: School care coordinators' reporting code cases
skills_to_grow: Acting on count alerts with judgement
role.ambitious_version: A counselor whose records keep themselves while they spend the time with students and families.

job.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
